Before we get to the HILLS, comment START to learn step by step how you can create and sell digital products. NOW THE HILLS: 1. Your product doesn’t need more pages. It needs a reason for someone to buy it. A 10-page guide that solves a specific problem can be more useful than a 100-page ebook full of information they could Google. 2. Being good at Canva isn’t enough. I was a graphic designer. Making things pretty was my thing. But you also need to explain who your product is for and why they need it. 3. Creating another product won’t fix avoiding marketing. If nobody knows about the first one, making five more just gives you five more things nobody knows about. 😅 4. You do NOT need to charge $7 just because you’re a beginner. Your experience level isn’t the only thing that determines the value of what you’re selling. 5. AI isn’t cheating. Use it to brainstorm, outline, and create. But review what it gives you. You’re still responsible for the product you put your name on. 6. Posting your offer once isn’t a sales strategy. You saw your post. That doesn’t mean every potential buyer did. Talk about your product again. Show how it works. Give people a reason to care. 7. Digital products can create passive income. Getting them to sell takes work. The product can be delivered while you sleep, but you still have to give people a reason to buy it. Ready to get started? Want to create and sell digital products? Here's what you actually do. 👇  1. Start with a problem. What problem are you solving for someone else? The best digital products make something easier, faster, or less overwhelming. 2. Create the solution. Turn what you know into something useful—a guide, checklist, planner, workbook, template, printable, mini-course, or resource. 3. Choose where to sell it. You can sell digital products through platforms like Etsy, Teachers Pay Teachers, Stan Store, or your own website. Choose the platform that makes sense for your product and audience. You can also publish them on Amazon Kindle Direct Publishing or Google Play.  4. Market it. Creating the product is only HALF the job. People have to find it! Use Pinterest, TikTok,  email, a blog, or search-friendly content to show people how your product solves their problem. 5. Learn from the first one...then create another. Your first product doesn't have to build financial freedom. It's your starting point. Create one useful product. Learn how to sell it. Improve. Then create another. Over time, you can build a collection of digital products that can be purchased while you're teaching, spending time with family, or simply living your life.  That's what I love about learning skills that can create income from home. I'm not looking for another job. I'm building more ways to earn—and more choices for my future. Financial freedom doesn't have to start with something huge. It can start with one product that solves one problem.
